- Avg tokens per request: 600 tokens (prompt + response)
- Effective reduction from KV/prefix caching: ~15–20% on repeat traffic
- Measurement window: 30-day rolling tokens

Maria — great questions, answered inline and added concrete numbers so your finance team can model them. See also the attached excel for line-item math.

1) Explicit baseline list prices (model profile = gen-large / inference profile we demoed):
   - US-hosted (no commit): $1,600 / 1M tokens (list)
   - EU-hosted (data & compute in EU, standard log retention 30d): $2,000 / 1M tokens (list) — this reflects a ~25% premium vs US

2) What drives the EU premium:
   - Compute/infra: EU cloud regions for reserved GPUs and regional networking add ~8–12% overhead.
   - Data residency and audit controls: additional engineering/ops separation, KMS/HSM usage and longer retention SLAs add ~5–10%.
   - Logging & egress: storing full content in EU increases storage and access controls costs; storing only minimal metadata (no content) can reduce the premium by ~6–10% depending on retention window.
   - Bottom line: If FinCo stores only metadata in EU and routes content processing to a redacted pipeline, we estimate EU premium could drop to ~12–15% (so EU list closer to $1,792–1,840 / 1M). We can model that in the quote.

3) Pilot and discounts:
   - Short pilot (5M/mo, month-to-month hosted) — typically no committed discount on list pricing.
   - We can do a pilot with a short-term reserved pool (minimum 1-month reservation at pilot volume) and offer a modest committed discount (example: 5% off list for a 1–3 month reserve at 5M/month). This is negotiable and depends on SLA needs.
   - For multi-month committed tiers (10M+/mo sustained) we move into the 5–15% discount band; deeper discounts for dedicated and longer-term contracts.

4) Timeline: noted — target to deliver a formal pricing appendix + DPA + SOC2 summary by EOD Thursday (tomorrow PDT). That gives you a week-plus to route to procurement ahead of end-of-Nov decision window.

Unit economics detail (assumptions attached in spreadsheet):
- Avg tokens per generation request: 600
- Baseline cache uplift (prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts): 18% effective token savings (we can isolate caching benefits per endpoint)
- Effective $/1M after 18% cache uplift (US list): $1,312 effective (i.e., list $1,600 * 0.82)

I've attached: draft-multiprice-quote-LOGAN-20261021.xlsx, redwood-pricing-sheet-20261021.pdf, soc2-summary-20261021.pdf.

If helpful I can also prepare two separate one-page quotes: (A) EU-residency (full content in EU) and (B) EU-metadata-only retention (compute in EU, content redaction). Which would you prefer for procurement to review?

Best,
Logan
